newsitem.title: UK: SECURE RETIREMENT TO BUY SOUTHAMPTON FC.
newsitem.headline: SECURE RETIREMENT TO BUY SOUTHAMPTON FC.

text.p: Secure Retirement Plc said on Tuesday it has agreed to buy English Premiership soccer club Southampton Football Club Ltd for 10.01 million pounds in a move which will recapitalise the club.

The deal, which is recommended by Southampton directors, would give the club increased access to funding together with a strengthened management team, residential property company Secure said in a statement to the London Stock Exchange.
Secure, chaired by Rupert Lowe, will rename itself Southampton Leisure Holdings Plc and plans to move the club's stadium to a 73-acre site in the north of Southampton, on the English south coast.
"We are aiming to create in Southampton a footballing force for the millennium and, in the new stadium, a focal point for the local community," Lowe said in the statement.

Southampton chairman Guy Askham, who will join the Secure board, said, "Secure is bringing to the table cash, assets, access to stock market funds and proven business skills. We have great ambitions for this club and this deal will play a very important part in achieving them."
Southampton is currently third from bottom of the Premiership, with just 13 points from 17 games.
Secure, trading in whose shares was suspended pending approval of the deal by shareholders, is offering 320 new Secure shares for every one Southampton share.
